hook.text: A building with an open ground floor — parking or shops — pancakes in an earthquake.

buildup.text: The soft story is weaker and more flexible than the floors above — a weak link.

discovery.text: All the earthquake deformation concentrates in the soft story — it fails catastrophically.

twist.text: San Francisco mandated soft-story retrofits after the 1989 Loma Prieta earthquake.

climax.text: Steel moment frames or braces are added to the open ground floor — stiffening the weak link.

punchline.text: A chain breaks at its weakest link. So does a building.

quiz.question: Why do soft-story buildings collapse in earthquakes?
options: The upper floors are too heavy for the foundation to support during shaking
The open, flexible ground floor concentrates all deformation and fails
Windows on the ground floor shatter and let shaking enter the building

details.summary: A soft story is a building level that is significantly less stiff or weaker than the stories above it, typically an open ground floor used for parking or commercial space.
details.whyItMatters: Soft-story collapse is one of the most common and lethal earthquake failure modes. Thousands of apartment buildings worldwide have this deadly vulnerability, and many cities have mandatory retrofit programs to address it.
takeaways: Open ground floors with fewer walls create a stiffness discontinuity
Deformation concentrates in the weak story, exceeding its capacity rapidly
San Francisco and Los Angeles require mandatory soft-story retrofits

faq.question: Why do soft-story buildings collapse while similar buildings without open ground floors survive?
faq.answer: When the ground floor is open for parking while upper floors have walls and partitions, the ground floor may be ten times less stiff. During shaking, nearly all lateral deformation concentrates in the soft story.

faq.question: How are soft-story buildings typically retrofitted?
faq.answer: Steel moment frames or braced frames are installed in the open ground floor to increase stiffness and ductility to match the upper stories. Plywood or steel plate shear walls can be added to existing framing. Foundation strengthening may be needed to resist the increased lateral forces.
